# Security policy

Fixture. The policy half of the matching pair. Both quotations are here, wrapped
at a different width, because word for word is about the words and a reflow of
one file is not drift.

## What a leaked link costs

This is the bound, in the same words as the threat model:

> Somebody holding a leaked link gets one account for each use
> the invitation had left, with exactly the template it carried.

## What a clone costs

> Two servers from one data directory both honour the same valid
> invitations, because neither knows the other exists.

## What is not defended

These are the entries the threat model marks as undefended, in the same words.

This second opening paragraph exists because it exists in the real policy.

A leaked link within its validity is an account for whoever found it.

An operator with administrator rights can mint whatever the ceilings allow.
